crowdhuman_characteristics.person_aspect: Full body / Upper body visible with high contrast

dense_video_characteristics.person_aspect: Top-down view of hair/heads with minimal body context
dense_video_characteristics.resolution: Compressed video stream with compression artifacts and motion blur

domain_comparison.domain_mismatch_findings: Significant domain gap observed. CrowdHuman contains street-level photos where faces and torsos are visible. The dense video features a top-down high-angle camera where people appear primarily as small circular heads without visible limbs or bodies.

head_annotation_analysis.technical_justification: In dense crowd videos with high-angle overhead cameras, body features are 80-90% occluded, leaving only heads visible. CrowdHuman hbox annotations directly isolate these exact head targets (mean size 36px in CrowdHuman), making head-target training technically aligned with overhead dense crowd scenes.

answers_to_core_questions.q1_explanation: Yes. Most visible heads/people in dense_crowd_test.mp4 have native pixel heights of 15-35px. When downscaled to imgsz=640, they shrink to 8-15px, occupying barely 1 to 1.5 stride-8 feature cells, falling below the detector's spatial activation threshold.
answers_to_core_questions.q2_explanation: Yes. 2x2 spatial tiling increases V2 average detections from 1.87 to 4.86 per frame and reduces zero-detection frames from 36.0% to 0.0%.
answers_to_core_questions.q3_explanation: Yes. CrowdHuman consists of eye-level DSLR street photographs showing torsos and faces. The dense crowd video is a high-angle overhead surveillance clip showing top-down heads with severe occlusion.
answers_to_core_questions.q4_explanation: No. VBOX still includes visible body/torso height (mean 200px in CrowdHuman). In high-angle dense crowds, bodies are completely occluded, so VBOX still forces the detector to look for upper body features that do not exist.
answers_to_core_questions.q5_explanation: Yes. CrowdHuman hbox annotations (mean size 36px) tightly isolate head regions without requiring torso/body visibility, matching the top-down head-only appearance in high-angle dense crowds.
answers_to_core_questions.q6_explanation: Yes. Global downscaling of large video frames to 640x640 destroys small spatial features. Spatial resolution (or tiling) combined with a head-specific detector architecture is required.
answers_to_core_questions.q7_next_recommended_experiment: Execute a controlled experiment testing head-target (HBOX) training combined with higher inference resolution or spatial tiling.
